reason: The cited evidence (E1-E3) focuses on CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloys, not duplex stainless steels, and does not address chromium segregation at grain boundaries or self-healing passive films. E3 shows higher Cr improves passivity, but this is a general trend, not specific support for the segregation mechanism. The key premises about segregation, self-healing, and applicability to duplex steels are unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Chromium segregation at grain boundaries can be enhanced in duplex stainless steels via thermo-mechanical processing.
Increased chromium at grain boundaries promotes formation of a stable Cr2O3-rich passive film.
A Cr2O3-rich passive film can self-heal and suppress localized corrosion like pitting.
Higher chromium content improves passivity and pitting resistance in chloride environments.
The proposed mechanism applies to duplex stainless steels under acidified chloride conditions at ~80°C.
